report.source_text: She was started on a nicardipine infusion with a systolic pressure goal of less than 120 and an esmolol infusion with a heart rate goal of less than 60. Cardiothoracic Surgery was consulted and she was taken to the operating room for emergent intervention. She spent 8 days in the hospital, during which she made a complete recovery and then was discharged.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Stanford Type A aortic dissection extending from aortic root to aortic bifurcation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old woman presented with abdominal and back pain along with rectal tenesmus and abdominal distention. Physical exam revealed diffuse abdominal tenderness but no pulse discrepancies. Contrast-enhanced CT angiography was performed and revealed a Stanford Type A aortic dissection extending from the aortic root to the aortic bifurcation. She was treated emergently with antihypertensives (nicardipine and esmolol) and underwent cardiothoracic surgical intervention, resulting in a complete recovery after 8 days of hospitalization.
